scope: Independent read-only review of six newly generated practice assets against their saved prompts and the current PRACTICE-BANKS standard.

assets.prompt_match: Seven requested objects, exact colors, no overlap or clipped object edges.
assets.labels: Top-row centers approximately14%,38%,62%,87% of width. Bottom-row centers24%,50%,78%. Use separate four/three row label positions rather than one uniform grid.
key_scaffolds: Treat keys as one set; do not require an exact count of individual overlapping keys.
Several blue objects exist, so one color clue may permit several answers. Add function/item evidence when a unique answer is required.
assets.white_paper_render: Viewed on white in browser; transparent backgrounds display cleanly without visible colored rectangular residue. Whole subjects retained.

visible_evidence.A: Adult pushing up from bed with feet on the floor.
visible_evidence.B: Adult at a glass office doorway; direction of movement is ambiguous.
visible_evidence.C: Adult eating cereal/toast with a cup in daylight.
visible_evidence.D: Two adults facing a visible television.

assets.prompt_match: Four intended activities and exact two-by-two composition; B is not unequivocally entering the office.
assets.labels: Standard2×2 positions A top-left, B top-right, C bottom-left, D bottom-right. Preserve faces and the TV.
key_scaffolds: Anchor B with a visible work-start timetable or fictional message; do not infer going to work rather than leaving from the pose alone.
Anchor getting up and breakfast with the supplied day-plan/times rather than treating food/daylight as infallible evidence.
assets.white_paper_render: Viewed native image; no clipping of task-bearing content. RGB background is intentional.

assets.prompt_match: Exactly three visible food types per box, matching all four requested combinations. All boxes and contents are complete.
assets.labels: Standard2×2 positions. Keep labels in gutters or on container rims, not over distinguishing food.
key_scaffolds: C contains one whole egg and two halves: do not count these as three eggs.
Tomato wedges and overlapping cheese slices do not establish exact whole-item counts.
B and D both have bread and cheese. A unique profile needs apple/banana or another discriminating condition.
Fish is identifiable in the taught limited set, but a menu text can remove ambiguity with other pale cooked meat.
assets.white_paper_render: Viewed native image; no clipping of task-bearing content. RGB background is intentional.

assets.prompt_match: Six requested objects and colors, whole garment edges and both shoes intact. Shirt and jacket are distinguished by buttons/collar versus zipper.
assets.labels: Standard3×2 positions. Do not let letter tags cover the narrow top collars or bottom jeans hems.
key_scaffolds: A pair of shoes is one vocabulary item in the code game, not one shoe.
Any code or price evidence must be live text and independently checked; avoid another naming-only introduction.

visible_evidence.top_left: Bedroom with one bed, bedside table and lamp.
visible_evidence.top_right: Bathroom with bathtub, toilet and sink.
visible_evidence.bottom_left: Kitchen/dining area with refrigerator, stove, sink, dining table and two blue chairs.
visible_evidence.bottom_right: Living area with sofa, armchair, coffee table, floor lamp and window unit.

assets.prompt_match: Four clear room zones and requested furniture. No visible door openings; this does not support a room-to-room walking-route puzzle.
assets.labels: Room centers approximately(28%,24%),(69%,22%),(25%,70%),(73%,68%). Put labels outside the objects or use short leaders.
key_scaffolds: There are three tables if bedside/dining/coffee tables all count; do not key a generic table count as two.
Two lamps are visible. The double-panel window may be described as one unit or two windows; avoid testing its exact count.
Refrigerator/stove/armchair are pictured but exceed the original6B assessed set. Provide a visible model before requiring these names.
Use clear room/furnishing decisions or memory rather than unsupported physical directions through absent doors.

visible_evidence.A: Man seated with hand on forehead.
visible_evidence.B: Woman seated with hand on stomach.
visible_evidence.C: Man seated holding ankle/boot with a leg across his knee.

assets.prompt_match: Three complete seated adults, heads/hands/feet and supporting seats inside the canvas. C supports a foot-area complaint with text, but is not an unambiguous bare-foot body-label reference.
assets.labels: Three separate figures left-to-right; add A–C outside the bitmap to avoid covering faces or feet.
key_scaffolds: Use first-person messages to specify headache, stomachache or a sore foot. The pose alone is not a medical diagnosis.
Foot versus leg is ambiguous from C alone; do not require ankle as newly memorized vocabulary.
Use the message/plan decision to consolidate language rather than a second body-picture naming lesson.

new_asset_freshness: All six are distinct new practice images and visually differ from the earlier core resources. Exact fresh artwork is necessary but not sufficient: the activity must be new consolidation, clue solving, memory, planning or decision work rather than another input-labeling presentation.
release_cautions: U3 office-entry direction needs text/timetable support.
U8 foot/leg needs a first-person message.
Check unique food-profile solutions and apartment counts against visible evidence.
